key_insight: A planner-executor multimodal AI system can answer many patient questions about lung cancer screening CT results while appropriately deferring out-of-scope questions to physicians.
clinical_relevance: This could improve patient understanding of screening results and support follow-up adherence, but it is designed to assist communication rather than replace clinician judgment.
method: Built a planner-executor multi-agent system to mimic clinical reasoning.
Used 116 lung cancer screening CT reports/images and an LLM-based framework to generate 699 simulated patient questions.
Evaluated tool-calling, self-regulation, and clinician-rated response quality.
evidence_signal: The system achieved 93.1% tool-calling accuracy and 92.6% self-regulation accuracy, with strong physician ratings for clinical accuracy and understandability on a subset of responses.
watch_item: Performance was tested on retrospective data and simulated questions, so real-world safety, generalizability, and workflow integration still need prospective validation.
paper_title: Planner-Executor Style Multimodal Agentic System to Answer Patient Questions in Lung Cancer Screening CT
